transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I feel like how I look and what I weigh is the only thing that matters about me now, and it’s starting to take over my life around food. It has just become really overwhelming, and I don't know how to stop obsessing over it.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food and feel out of control, and if so, do you then try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?

Yes, on bad nights it's like a switch flips and I lose all control, tearing through huge amounts of bread, chips, and leftovers in my kitchen. Afterward, I feel so guilty that I force myself to throw up to 'undo the damage' or I'll skip meals, and this cycle has been happening at least a couple of times a week.

Compared with what would be expected for your age and height, is your weight currently very low or have you been significantly underweight recently? If you know it, please tell me your height and current weight.

I don't know my exact height and weight off the top of my head, and I'm not really sure if my weight would be considered significantly low. Though, lately, friends and family have been commenting on how lean I look.

Have you missed periods, felt faint or unusually cold, or had a doctor tell you that you are underweight because of restricting food? Also, between these binge-and-purge episodes, are you mostly eating very little to keep your weight down?

Well, I'm a man, so missed periods don't apply, and I haven't felt unusually cold or faint, nor has a doctor told me I'm underweight. But yes, between those bad nights I restrict myself heavily, skipping meals or sticking strictly to plain chicken and vegetables because I'm so terrified of gaining weight.

Have you recently been told by a clinician that you are underweight or significantly below a healthy weight for your height, or do your clothes fit much more loosely than before? This helps me tell whether the bingeing and purging are happening while you are at a very low weight.

I haven't seen a doctor about my weight before today, so I've never been told I'm underweight. While my family has commented on me looking "lean," I don't feel like my clothes are fitting extremely loose, and my main focus is just doing whatever I can to prevent any weight gain.

Before these binge-and-purge episodes started, had your weight dropped to a clearly underweight level for your height because you were restricting food? If you know it, what is your current height and weight?

I'm not sure if my weight actually dropped to a level that would be considered clinically underweight, though friends and family did comment that I looked "lean" around that time. I also don't know my exact current height or weight off the top of my head.

At your lowest during this time, did you look or feel clearly underweight—for example, bones sticking out, needing smaller clothes, or other people being worried you were too thin? Or were you mostly in a normal weight range despite the bingeing, vomiting, and restricting?

I honestly don't know if I was technically underweight or just in a normal range. Nobody seemed worried that I was too thin, they just commented that I looked "lean." For me, it was more about the constant panic of seeing the scale go up even a tiny bit rather than looking skeletal.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control, followed by compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting and fasting/restriction occurring at least a couple of times per week. Self-evaluation is excessively influenced by weight and shape. There is no clear evidence that these behaviors occur exclusively during a period of significantly low body weight, making bulimia nervosa the best fit over anorexia nervosa binge-purge subtype.
